title: Error-Correcting Codes (Sloane & Grassl Open World Tables)
tagline: Live A(n,d) & A(n,d,w) world-record hunts · Lean 4.36.0 kernel
question: How many 17-bit words can pairwise differ in at least 6 positions?
description: Formalize the Hamming code, the sphere-packing and Plotkin bounds in pure Lean 4, then hunt the open entries of Brouwer's live code tables: the general binary code A(17,6) (best known 258, upper bound 340), the constant-weight code A(17,6,7) (best known 166, upper bound 206), and the constant-weight code A(20,8,10) (best known 176, upper bound 206). Every larger code is checked by the Lean kernel in about 1–2 seconds.
verdict: open world record hunt — accepting token donations.

tug_of_war.disclaimer: Counts Lean-verified explicit codes vs. Lean-verified upper bounds (sphere-packing, Plotkin, ¬ Record certificates).

objectives.title: Hamming Code, Sphere-Packing & Plotkin Bounds
objectives.finish_line: Verify the Hamming [7,4,3] code (16 codewords), prove Hamming's sphere-packing bound |C|·(n+1) ≤ 2^n for distance-3 codes (so A(7,3) = 16 exactly), and prove the Plotkin bound |C|·(2d−n) ≤ 2d.

objectives.title: Claim the Hills: Lean-Certify the Classical Record Codes
objectives.finish_line: Lean-verify the classical launch-floor codes: the padded Nordstrom–Robinson code A(17,6) ≥ 256, the Golay-derived A(17,6,7) ≥ 166 and the group code A(20,8,10) ≥ 176.

objectives.title: Open World Record Frontier: Beat Brouwer's Tables for A(17,6), A(17,6,7) & A(20,8,10)
objectives.finish_line: Find a code larger than any published one: A(17,6) ≥ 259 (record 258, upper bound 340), A(17,6,7) ≥ 167 (record 166, upper bound 206), or A(20,8,10) ≥ 177 (record 176, upper bound 206).
